card.title: Specific latent heat of fusion and vaporization

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Specific latent heat is the heat per unit mass for a change of state at constant temperature, Q = m L. Fusion covers melting and freezing. Vaporization covers boiling and condensation. A path that both changes state and changes temperature needs an m L term and an mc Δθ term.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Values of L depend on the pressure. The quoted values are for standard atmospheric pressure.  ·  Sublimation, solid to gas, has its own latent heat.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Specific latent heat L is the heat absorbed or released when 1 kg of a substance changes state at constant temperature. The heat is Q = m L, and there is no Δθ term while the change of state is going on.  ·  The specific latent heat of fusion, L_f, is for melting or freezing. For ice at 0°C it is about 3.34 × 10^5 J/kg. Melting absorbs this heat. Freezing releases it.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Latent heat of fusion  ·  Latent heat of vaporization  ·  Q = m L  ·  Constant temperature

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Latent heat changes the state at constant temperature.  ·  Fusion is solid to liquid.  ·  Vaporization is liquid to gas.  ·  L is heat per unit mass.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Heat Q = mcΔT; specific heat c, thermal capacity C = mc, heat capacity per mole = C. molar.  ·  Latent heat L: Q = mL (change of state at constant T). Calorimetry: heat lost = heat gained.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: What stays constant during boiling?

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: How much heat melts 0.20 kg of ice at 0°C and then warms the water to 20°C? Take L_f = 3.34 × 10^5 J/kg and c = 4200 J kg^-1 K^-1.

rows.text: During melting, the temperature → B  ·  Q for vaporizing a mass m is → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: The specific latent heat of vaporization, L_v, is for boiling or condensation. For water at 100°C it is about 2.26 × 10^6 J/kg, several times larger than L_f, because the molecules must be separated much further.  ·  During melting the temperature stays at the melting point until all the solid has changed. The supplied energy increases the potential energy of the molecules, not the average kinetic energy that temperature tracks.  ·  A warming problem that crosses a change of state is done in pieces: mc Δθ up to the change point, then m L, then mc Δθ in the new state. Leaving out m L is the usual error.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ heat q = mcδt; specific heat c, thermal capacity c = mc, heat capacity per mole = c. molar..  ·  Latent heat is not specific heat. One happens at constant temperature.  ·  Steam at 100°C carries extra energy m L_v that water at 100°C does not.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: L_f and L_v are properties of the substance and the change, not of the mass. The mass sits outside, in Q = m L.  ·  The temperature does not rise while ice is still melting in the mixture.  ·  Do not multiply L by a temperature change.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Keep ice at 0°C and steam at 100°C unless the question moves them further.  ·  Write Q = m L and say what each symbol means.  ·  Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Finish with the number, the unit, and the direction when the quantity has one.  ·  Newton's law of cooling: rate of heat loss ∝ (T − T₀); dθ/dt = −k(θ − θ₀).  ·  State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Limit to remember: heat q = mcδt; specific heat c, thermal capacity c = mc, heat capacity per mole = c. molar.  ·  The same L applies to the reverse change. Condensing 1 kg of steam at 100°C releases m L_v, which is why a steam burn is severe compared with a burn from water at the same temperature.  ·  # Specific latent heat of fusion and vaporization ## 1.
